anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Roasted with fire, not boiled in water.

pass_a_gloss: Well then is the Holy Spirit called fire, which having taken up we must converse with the fleshes of Christ, I mean the divine writings, so that through this spiritual fire having roasted them we may eat them roasted with fire; for by such a fire the sayings will be altered, and we shall see the sweet and nourishing of them, not boiling with worse water.
pass_b_english: Rightly then is the Holy Spirit called fire, which we must take up and then converse with the flesh of Christ — I mean the divine scriptures — so that through this spiritual fire [we may roast them and eat them roasted with fire. For by such a fire the words will be changed, and we shall see what is sweet and nourishing in them, not boiling them with worse water.]
source_text: Καλῶς οὖν λέγεται πῦρ τὸ ἅγιον πν(εῦμ)α, <ὃ> ἀναλαβόντας ἡμᾶς δεῖ προσομιλῆσαι ταῖς σαρξὶν τοῦ Χ(ριστο)ῦ, λέγω δὲ ταῖς θείαις γραφαῖς, ἵνα διὰ τούτου τοῦ πν(ευματ)ικοῦ πυρὸς|| [ὀπτήσαντες αὐτὰς φάγωμεν ὀπτὰς πυρί· ἀλλοιωθήσεται γὰρ διὰ τοῦ τοιούτου πυρὸς τὰ ῥητά, καὶ τὸ ἡδὺ καὶ τρόφιμον αὐτῶν ὀψόμεθα, μὴ συνέψοντες ὕδατι χείρονι·
